criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: Specific dated opener (June 18 FERC, six named RTOs) with a clean structural consequence for Alaska. Two-sentence hook runs ~219 chars, just past the ~210 see-more cutoff.

criteria.name: Industry relevance
criteria.notes: Every thread carries an AK angle plus a named consequence and dollar figure (FERC governance gap, STAK $500M, DAF June 29, NDAA $2.6B). NDAA AI tie is labeled analytical.

criteria.name: Factual density
criteria.notes: Named specifics at nearly every sentence in the evidence paragraph; analytical paragraphs appropriately sparse.

criteria.name: Source quality
criteria.notes: FERC lead rests on two trade sources (Utility Dive, Construction Dive) with FERC.gov primary unresolved (403); AK/Railbelt tie is analytical and correctly framed. NDAA has a verified primary (Sullivan release); STAK has a DNR primary; DAF on two secondaries.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Reads like post_001.md: analytical, position-taking, structural; self-aware ‘that’s my read, not a claim anyone briefed’ matches the anchor register.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: 2-4 sentence paragraphs, ~430 words, ~2.6k chars under cap; the evidence paragraph is dense but scannable.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Real, debatable closing question naming four distinct actors, tied to the missing-rulebook tension.

criteria.name: Business actionability
criteria.notes: A utility exec, RCA commissioner, developer, or allocator can name the governance gap and the live calendar pressure (DAF June 29, STAK finding) as a decision trigger.

one_sentence_fix: Seek a direct FERC.gov docket URL or release number for the June 18 large-load interconnection action so the lead rests on a verified primary rather than two trade secondaries.
